#script: # WHY A LIST AND NOT A DERIVATION: the caller of a clock is a crontab line on
# another machine. Nothing in this tree can see one -- realisateur#511 scanned
# bin/ and .github/ for callers, found none for monkey-watch.sh, and deleted a
# live observer whose invoker was dexter's crontab. A CRON_TAG derivation only
# finds the clocks that install themselves, which is every clock except the one
# that stacked. So the off-host callers are WRITTEN DOWN, and cron-lock.test.sh
# holds both halves: every row here takes the lock, and every script that does
# declare a CRON_TAG has a row.

where the caller lives: NO LIVE CALLER. monkey was deleted 2026-09-24 and the `*/10` line came out of dexter's crontab at 02:26Z the next morning (backup: dexter ~/crontab.pre-monkey-delete.20260925T022655Z). The row stays because the file still declares a CRON_TAG and cron-lock.test.sh C grades that; the file itself is now residue and reaping it is its own pass.
dexter crontab; the line its own --cadence prints. Zach installs it -- an agent cannot arm this host's cron.

monkey root crontab, by hand -- tag realisateur:unarmed:CADENCE, no --install-cadence. #894 made unarmed.sh the verb `unarmed`, off carries.tsv's libexec/ rows and prop_host_tools() -- the live crontab row still invokes /usr/local/libexec/selfdev/unarmed.sh by its old path (unrefreshed now, since nothing carries it there anymore) and needs a follow-up host-side repoint to `unarmed --check`, which this dispatch does not perform (root crontab edit, out of scope here)
